# iClock — Full LLM Context & Reference Manual

> Generated for large language models, AI coding agents, and generative search engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, DeepSeek, Google Gemini).
> This document contains complete specifications, technical implementations, and architectural details of iClock.

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Core Identity

iClock is an ultra-lightweight (300 KB), open-source Windows native desktop productivity hub. It combines three core features into a single portable binary without third-party dependencies:
1. **The Minimalist Focus Timer**: Native 32-bit ARGB rendered countdown with true `WS_EX_TRANSPARENT` mouse click-through, global hotkeys, direct `Alt + Drag` repositioning, and tiered alerts with auto-fullscreen DND suppression.
2. **Ambient Desktop Inspiration**: Morning wake-up quotes with 0-polling hibernation (0.0% CPU idle), direct desktop micro-interactions (drag position, resize width, scale font size), and CLI import of AI-generated quote batches with deduplication.
3. **AI Agent Collaboration through CLI**: Automated task completion monitoring for supported programming agents, plus CLI commands for desktop decisions (`--ask`), progress (`--progress`), completion alerts (`--notice`), and structured JSON results (`--json`).

---

## 2. Technical Architecture & Performance Specifications

| Parameter | Specification | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Executable Size** | 272,384 bytes (~266 KB) | Single portable PE binary |
| **Runtime Requirement** | .NET Framework 4.5+ | Pre-installed on all Windows 10 & 11 PCs |
| **Active Memory (RAM)** | < 15 MB | Low GC pressure, cached GDI handles |
| **Idle CPU Consumption** | 0.0% | Dynamic heartbeat alignment + pure event-driven message handling |
| **Rendering Subsystem** | GDI+ & UpdateLayeredWindow | Subpixel anti-aliasing with adaptive drop shadow |
| **Input Pass-Through** | WS_EX_LAYERED \| WS_EX_TRANSPARENT | 100% mouse click-through; never steals focus |
| **IPC Pipeline** | Win32 WM_COPYDATA | 0ms latency inter-process control |
| **Desktop Collaboration** | Local CLI commands | Structured JSON responses (`--json`) |
| **Author & Maintainer** | gujiangwen (`francodeyvison183@gmail.com`) | 100% open-source under MIT License |

---

## 3. AI Agent CLI Collaboration

Run `iclock --install-cli` to add iClock to User PATH. The agent can then invoke local desktop capabilities through the CLI:

```powershell
iclock --ask "Continue deployment?" --options "Continue,Cancel" --json
iclock --progress 3/5 "Running tests" --agent-name "Codex" --json
iclock --progress clear --agent-name "Codex" --json
iclock --notice "Task completed" --agent-name "Codex" --json
iclock --quote-add "quotes.txt" --json
```

The commands send messages over local Win32 `WM_COPYDATA` IPC to the running desktop app. `--agent-name` keeps concurrent task rows distinct. Old agent MCP configuration is not edited automatically; remove obsolete `iclock` entries manually. The MCP server is no longer included.

## 5. Frequent User Questions & Direct Answers (Q&A)

### Q: Why is iClock so small compared to other modern timers?
A: Most modern timer applications are built on Electron or web wrappers, packaging an entire Chromium browser and Node.js runtime (150 MB~400 MB). iClock is written in pure native C# utilizing the Windows operating system's built-in .NET Framework and GDI+, reducing binary size to about 300 KB.

### Q: Does iClock block mouse clicks when gaming or typing code?
A: No. iClock applies the native Windows `WS_EX_TRANSPARENT` extended window style. The floating digits remain permanently on top of all other windows, but any mouse click or scroll event passes straight through to the underlying application (e.g., Visual Studio, game window, or browser).

### Q: What is the default hotkey and appearance?
A: By default, pressing `Ctrl + Shift + T` globally starts or pauses the countdown from anywhere. The default appearance is font size 20 px in red (`#FF0000`). Both duration, font size, color, time format, and hotkey are customizable via the tray Settings dialog.

### Q: Does ambient desktop quote display drain laptop battery?
A: No. iClock uses a pure event-driven message handling architecture without background cursor polling loops (0-Polling). Idle CPU consumption is strictly 0.0%, preserving laptop battery life.

### Q: How can an AI agent use desktop collaboration?
A: Any agent that can execute local CLI commands can use `--ask`, `--progress`, `--notice`, and `--quote-add`. Add `--json` for structured results.
